measured_gap.command: for s in $(git rev-list --first-parent --merges -20 origin/main); do git diff-tree --cc -r --name-only $s; done
measured_gap.observed: 19 of the 20 most recent first-parent merges on origin/main report no paths. c31b8ee191e1704a5ebca70e60e178b97a433d99 reports docs/06_status/lanes/UTV2-1514.json — content present in neither parent, at a path that is ALLOW_PATTERNS[0].
measured_gap.significance: This is the gap the lane closes, measured on the real branch rather than constructed. The shipped C1-C4 set classifies an incoming merge by the paths it touches and never looks at the content now at those paths, so it admits this merge.

mutation_control.command: apply each mutation to the real source, run the affected suites, restore byte-for-byte
mutation_control.expected: the decisive inversion is that the shipped condition set verifies a real evil merge
mutation_control.observed: M1 C5 removed -> still REFUSED (C6, C7 catch it). M2 C6 removed -> still REFUSED (C5, C7 catch it). M3 C5+C6+C7 removed, i.e. the set UTV2-1836 shipped -> VERIFIED on a real branch-side evil merge built in a real git repository. M4 C1's rev-list --not cross-check disabled -> 29/29 collector tests still pass. M5 C1's per-parent walk reverted to parents[1] only -> 2 tests fail, including the real-git octopus case.
mutation_control.honest_reading: M1 and M2 did not individually flip the verdict, because on a branch-side evil merge all three new conditions fire and removing one leaves two. The inversion that demonstrates the gap is M3, and it is recorded as it came out rather than as it would read better. M4 shows the rev-list cross-check is redundant: the premise it was written against — that a two-parent merge whose second parent is on main can carry off-main commits through that parent's ancestry — is false, since everything reachable from an ancestor of main is an ancestor of main. It is kept as a second independently computed answer and its source comment says exactly that. The load-bearing half of the C1 change is the per-parent walk, which M5 proves.

reserved_surface_untouched.significance: No workflow, and therefore no gate, references any of this. The Merge Gate integration is written as a proposal in verification.md and is deliberately not applied. PM authorization of 2026-09-05 is to prepare and verify, not to activate an unreviewed merge-policy change.

receipt_is_output_not_input.detail: Every value this lane adds is recomputed from git or the GitHub API. None is parsed from a comment, a file or a workflow input. The pre-existing collector test asserting that a previously posted receipt is never read back as evidence still passes. A receipt accepted as an input would be forgeable by anyone with comment access, which is the failure this mechanism must not create.

local_verify_limitation.significance: Not a failure of this change. `verify` is a && chain, so reaching its final stage establishes that verify:static — env check, lint, type-check, build, test, command manifest, migration lint — exited 0. The CI receipt is authoritative for the stage that cannot run here.

known_gaps: C7 cannot be computed for an empty PR diff and reports as unavailable rather than as a match, so two unrelated empty diffs can never read as identical to each other.

C6's anchor is `git merge-base <head> origin/<base>`, not origin/main's tip. This is a deliberate divergence from the issue's literal wording: the tip moves on a schedule via the readiness ledger, so anchoring to it would make C6 an always-refuse control, which acceptance item 5 explicitly guards against. Recorded in the source comment and in diff-summary.md.
The rev-list cross-check inside C1 is redundant (mutation M4) and is documented in-source as redundancy rather than as a catch it does not have.
